Every corridor, every chamber, bears witness to the burstiness of a bygone epoch, a tapestry woven with threads of intrigue and wonder. It beckons explorers to fathom its perplexing depths, forever challenging the boundaries of human comprehension.

One of the great historical site of the world. Use the guide to get more details about the placeb& the history (there is not enough written information on the display so you need to rely on the guide).

After coming here i can only say Xi'an and the Emperor's tomb is the 1st place i should have visited in China. Do not omit to visit the 2nd part including additional tombs and the museum of the bronze chariots, using the bus starting from the entrance of the main museum.
A must see when in Xi'an! The museum is very well organised and easy to navigate. The number of statues is astonishing
Just too many people... but still, you must go take a look at it if you are at Xi'an...

Extremely interesting to see, though it is often very crowded and can be quite difficult to squeeze your way in to view anything. People even bring umbrellas inside and I copped at least two to the eyes. One tip I would give to prospective visitors who have never been to China before is to just push in. Nobody lines up here, so if you're at the back of a line, you're a sucker! This place is quite far away from Xi'an city, so be prepared for a long taxi ride. The average cost as at the time of writing this was about 120-150 Yuan. If the driver wants to charge you more, you're paying the white tax and should haggle them down. Taxis will absolutely not run the meter for such a jourey so keep this in mind. The exhibition and museum itself is very interesting, and a must for anybody interested in Chinese history, culture or archaeology.

Much bigger than I expected. Super super super super super crowded. It's like playing bumper pinball with people but everyone should see this place. one of the pits was so big that you could put three a380s end-to-end and still have room.
Reccomended to arrive when it opens as it can get extremely busy. Would also reccomend the audio guide or a tour guide as there isn't much to read in the pits about the history itself
Amazing place to visit and good to see the state of untouched Terracotta Pieces. What a woundful place. Just a shame they didn't look after the farmers who found the discovery

One word... Amazing. Only part of the whole site is unearthed as the scientists and archaeologists cannot solve the oxidixation problem where the colours on the terracotta warriors will fade when exposed to our atmosphere. Well worth the visit. Met the old chinese man who unearthed the warriors.

Went here quite some time ago. A night's train ride from Beijing to Xian where, finding a bus to go to this site was fairly easy-but cold in the winter. Well worth the round trip. The mere SCALE of this, which is still being unearthed is stunning. Standing face to face with the exhumed soldiers, the detail is amazing. Walking the pits where the warriors remained in the ground can take hours.

Folks, this is NOT the Terracotta Warriors. The Qin shi huang mausoleum is a totally different thing. Your ticket to the Terracotta Warriors includes this attraction but you need to take a 10 minute shuttle (free) from the Terracotta Warriors to this site. Once you arrive, you get a free guide for 45 minutes (chinese). This site is huge though. You will get lost and waste a lot of time if you don't have any sense of direction. There isn't much to see here as the mausoleum is not excavated. It's just a massive mound and a tombstone.

This is the place you definitely want visit if you go to Xi'an City, it is amazing. From culture/history pointy of view, Terracotta Army and the Great Wall are two must-go sites in China. Not far from Xi'an City (one to two hour ride), one day trip is good for most people.
It took 3 hours to walk inside here very huge place get ready a wheel chair for citizen yeahhh
Obviously it's a 5. Can be very busy but if you wait a minute the large guided groups move on and leave plenty of space to get the photos you want.

Just a tip: get there as early as possible, because it gets uncomfortable around lunchtime. It is a huge arial with 3 pits and food miles, the mausoleum of the emperor is not to be recommended because it is totally far away and also the carriage of the bronze statue is not so big.
Amazing! I feel so grateful to visit Qin Emperor’s graveyard. The museum has provided free bus to the graveyard. Try to catch the bus before 17.00 p.m.

(Visited August 2017) The history alone leaves you speechless and then you walk in.. WOW! Pure shock and awe. Such a site to see! The detail that goes into every single one to make each soldier an individual amongst the sea of many. Amazing craftsmanship. Very VERY crowed so make sure you make that effort to nudge forward to take in the beautiful site and history. A must visit if in Xi'an and listen to the guides, very good info and understanding of how the statues are built and if they broke during assembly...

A must visit when u r in China. It is a super large collection of life-size terra cotta sculptures in battle formations, reproducing the mega imperial guard troops of Emperor Qin Shi Huang (259 - 210BC), the first emperor of the first unified dynasty of Imperial China. Being the most significant archeological excavations of the 20th century and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the Terracotta Army is no doubt a must-see for every visitor to Xi'an.

I loved every moment of this, I visiting the terracotta army was well worth the visit. There is 3 big pits or hangers and a exhibition hall which is like the museum part of it. We went part of a tour but that meant we ended up going to some tourist trap places trying to sell souvenirs for high prices but made it a lot easier to get there and you don't have to buy anything from them.

if you visit Xi'an probably is because you want to is it Terracotta warriors ;) so this place is a must see once in Xi'an! from main train station hop on bus 307, is a public bus and takes about 40min / 1 hour to arrive at destination! be careful cause they try ( i don't know why since is a public bus) to visit the nearby mausoleum.. just avoid it (unless you are interested) and head to Terracotta warriors! before entering the building you'll have 5 minutes walking in a beauti5park/entrance! at the exit you'll find yourself in a shopping mall ;) expect to spend an entire morning or at least 3 hours

We bought the 2 entrance tickets to Terracotta army and Mausoleum, online. Then we took a premium taxi (Didi) from Xian downtown to the Terracotta Army location. This is much cheaper and more flexible arrangement than joining a tour. There is an audio guide so we could follow the 'story' of the place and history behind all that. We bought tickets to go on a ride around the mausoleum, which is a vast complex (feeling tired after long walks in Terracotta army site, a different site to the mausoleum). We spend about 2 hours to see all we can see there, most time was spent to queue for the ride. The king horses exhibition is worth seeing, especially for a materials engineer like me. Amazing materisls technology for c200 BC. Great place to go, but just too crowded to enjoy the exhibition.

Amazing place, and fascinating story behind it all. I'd recommend going with a guide to get the full back story of this place. We also visited the terracotta factory before going here, which is where they replicate the process of how the warriors were made. It's also a great place where you can buy miniature Terra cotta warriors in real clay, not plastic. At a great price. At the time it was ¥120 for 3 figures. Which I've yet to find a better price anywhere. Yuyuan old street in Shanghai sells individual ones for ¥50 each, which is cheaper if you're only buying one, but more expensive if you want a set with different ones.

If you want to avoid the crowd of this museum, go in early morning. This museum open at 08.30. We became the first one to enter this museum and its not crowded. One hour later, the tourist start to flock on this musem. Wear comfortable shoes and clothes, you will need to walk a lot. Dont loose your ticket because you have to show it twice. Summer is the peak of this museum according to our tour guide, but the heat can reach 40degC, do dont forget to check the weather and bring equipment accordingly. If you can afford the tour guide, it is better to be with tour guide because you will understand more about the history behind Terracota army. There a lot of souvenir shops around, but it is cheaper in Xian Muslim Street.

It's pretty impressive, but overcrowded. We went first thing in the morning and stayed untill noon. Around 11:00am many groups are leaving, so I would recommend to go a bit later in the day to avoid the crowds.
Great introduction to the history of the terracotta warriors. Would highly recommend a visit before hand. Lots to by, much with certificates of authenticity.
Unique, this must be experienced. Everything is perfectly organized. If anyone goes to Xian, be sure to visit this archeological site of the Tarakota Warriors.

It was a place that I wanted to go, so it left a deep impression for me. Enterence fee is 120RMB and a voice guide rental fee is 30RMB. After watching Bingmayong then you have to go Tomb of the Qin Shi Huang. There have a shuttle bus.
This is the most beautiful place in Xi’an and it is worth visiting! It was impressive!

Probably one of the most amazing place to visit in China. But, the place was so crowded with their own locals, not many foreigner visit there. However, they have english guide device for foreigners, which is quite helpful and automated whenever we reached the guided location. Very interesting. The only downside is the other museum wasn't so interesting compare to the main one, as they show almost similar attraction and some historical things.
If you like the history of China, this is a must-see place. I had an amazing tour guide(Linda), which made it more pleasant and understandable.
Definitely worth the visit. Unique place with nothing else compared to it anywhere in the world. Find a good certified tour guide to explain the details to you.

The Terracotta Army is a wonder, so much history in one little location. I was definitely underwhelmed by the statues but the more you read the better. If we didnt go to Huashan, I would think our trip to Xi'an was only ok. There are many people and not everything is in English, which is fine. Dont expect to be with just your group. A must if you are in the area.

Amazing historic discovery. Thos place is a must see just remember you need to hire a tour guide any language. Tips if you are 60 and over holding foreign passport you need to pay 120 rmb but if you hold a id from hong kong it is free for senior.
A must visited landmark in Xi’An! While it is super crowded, it is definitely worthwhile.

A fascinating live excavation site. Amazing seeing the 2200 year old terracotta army in their original setting, each soldier has incredible detail and all 8000 are unique. 40km from Xi'an, well organised site - but busy. Recommend having a guide to explain the intracies as there is limited English signage. You need at least 2 hours on a day that is not a local holiday - my guide told me to double that if it is a holiday. I estimate that the foreigners only accounted for 1% of the visitors on the day I was there. There are no ticketing facilities on site - must be pre booked.

A very important place to visit to understand Chinese history. Takes 1,5 hours with a guide. Just enough and not too much. Good for a 2 days trip to Xi’an. With 10 million annual visitors- it is crowded.
This is a must when in Shaanxi! It is a short trip from Xi'an with many transit options. The magnitude of the site will leave you speachless.

The pits were fantastic and absolutely mind blowing! If you are into museums there is plenty to look at bit the warriors them selves were amazing. Expect large crowds! We didn't have a guide but most of the information was also in English which made it even better!

Buying tickets on trip.com saves some money. The crowds in pit 1 and 2 cannot be really avoided, unless you come very early or late. I also recommend to check out the museum for seeing close ups of the warriors.
